metrics.method: Full history read message-by-message (1041 lines, 2025-07-24 to 2026-09-03). Client = sender 'Eli' per config/clients.yaml client_aliases; everyone else (team.yaml, vendor chat teams, and Sophie Logan / Raw Agency) counted as our side. client_questions_total = distinct client asks requiring a reply (interrogatives plus explicit 'please confirm / let me know' requests), counted per thread not per message, so a multi-message ask counts once. unanswered_over_24h = those threads where no substantive team reply landed within 24h, including 4 never answered at all (Mica kickoff-call slot 2025-08-08, Michelle's scope 2025-09-08, IG 'not recommended' 2026-03-17, suspicious login 2026-03-18) and the Halloween/collab upload thread she asked three times across 2025-10-22 to 10-27; a tag-someone-else or a question back does not count as an answer. max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive non-service messages from our side (2026-05-05 to 2026-06-01, 27 days). promises = explicit datable commitments by our side ('I'll…', 'we will…', a stated recurring cadence); 1 of the 34 (Lissy's onboarding-manager role) scored partial and is excluded from both kept and lapsed.

'I would like to receive the content ideas / scripts so it’s easier for me to make content I know exactly what content you need!' (2025-09-09); 'im on my content trip in Cancun... Please let me know what content you guys need' (2025-10-03). She reliably delivers when told exactly what is needed — the 99 voice notes, the Halloween set, the collab.
what_worked: DMCA takedowns done the whole way: named owner, an ETA, and an unprompted close-the-loop. Nick reported the impersonators, said 'ETA on these removals will be 2-8 days' (2025-12-07), then posted 'The Facebook accounts are now down ☑️' (2025-12-08). Her reply — 'Amazing thank you Nick great job 👏' (2025-12-11) — is the warmest praise in 14 months. This is the template for every other workstream and it is the one we silently stopped (last report 2026-03-04).

Sophie Logan's cadence in Sept–Oct 2025: a real call, a written debrief, a bi-weekly report and a 14-day game plan she could actually act on. 'Was a pleasure you so nice!! ❤️ thank you for sending this over too xx' (2025-09-18). It ended without explanation on 2025-10-27 and nothing replaced it.

The week of 2026-08-30 proves the fix is cheap: Mayson shipped the content Drive, escalated the deleted-accounts issue twice until someone engaged, and closed her hanging question himself; Stephski closed the reconciliation, credited the $2,499.59 overpayment and correctly sequenced the next invoice after it. Her tone reverted within days — 'Thank you for sending this over' (2026-09-02) — from the only edged message on record a week earlier.
top_fix: Give this account one named owner with a written 24-hour rule: every client message gets either a substantive answer or a named owner plus an ETA within 24 hours, and every open item — IG recovery status, money received, what a flag actually means — gets an unprompted written update with a number or a date until it is closed. Nearly every failure here is the same failure: somebody said 'on it' and nobody's job was to come back and say what happened. Do it first for the three deleted Instagram accounts, and while doing it, ask her to delete the 2026-08-31 credentials message and rotate all three passwords.
